answer: For protein-coding genes only (n = 19,942), the Pearson correlation coefficient between gene length and gene expression (per-gene mean of raw batch-corrected read counts across all 723 samples) is r ≈ 0.050 (r = 0.050383, p ≈ 1.09e-12) — a weak positive correlation. Supplementary notes: (a) with log1p-transformed mean expression, r = 0.320356 (p < 1e-300), showing the raw-counts correlation is driven mainly by a few extremely highly expressed long genes; (b) excluding the 645 protein-coding genes with all-zero expression, r = 0.045979 (n = 19,297, p ≈ 1.66e-10), essentially unchanged.
